fields.v: RSCB-MC (Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandit with Memory Control), implemented in the pythalab-codex-issue-memory artifact (commit 227bbe3, Python 3.12.3); no release version

Pattern-variant-episode issue-memory records (canonical root-cause pattern, context-specific variants with command/path/stack signatures, validated episodes); fixed 16-feature state vector (Table 1); action set of 7 actions (no memory, top1 resolution, top3 summary, high-precision retrieval, high-recall retrieval, abstain, ask feedback); risk-sensitive reward (false-positive penalty γ=4.0 > verified α=2.0 > accepted β=1.0). No specification document

Normalize debugging context to query profile; retrieve candidate memories; build 16-feature state; score each action (Eq. 17); safety override (replace unsafe injection by abstain/no memory); apply action; observe feedback; compute reward; update policy (Algorithm 1)

fields.v: Tasks: seeded smoke-scale artifacts (queries, paraphrases, hard negatives, replay events). Configurations: retrieval baselines (lexical, static hybrid, static hybrid + abstention, full retriever) and bandit baselines (epsilon-greedy, UCB1, Thompson, LinUCB, risk-sensitive Thompson) vs RSCB-MC, oracle upper bound. Held constant: same artifacts and seeds, deterministic scripts. Acceptance criterion: proxy labels from replay metadata. Repetitions: 2 deterministic seeds. Human intervention: none

RSCB-MC best non-oracle replay success (62.5% vs 60.0% risk-sensitive TS, 50.0% static) with 0.0% FP (static 17.5%); 5 points below oracle; 0% FP on hard negatives vs 75% static hybrid; sub-millisecond p95 latency. No significance tests

Distinguished methods on FP and proxy success; canonical retrieval saturated (all 100%), so it did not distinguish retrieval methods. Deterministic, so repeatable. Limitations stated: smoke scale, offline replay not causal, proxy labels, reward magnitude may not alter action selection

Smoke-scale evidence only; offline replay is not a causal online evaluation; hot-path labels are proxies; context-budget and dry-run experiments are proxy tasks; single-step bandit does not model delayed multi-turn effects or memory aging; controller over-conservative (wrong abstentions); inherits stale/contradictory memory. Future: full-scale benchmark, live LLM-agent evaluation, calibration, off-policy evaluation, long-horizon modeling

Abstract and conclusion highlight 62.5% / 0.0% FP; the 'agent dry-run' experiment mentioned in limitations (p. 22) is not reported in results. Abstention text (p. 15) says RSCB-MC 'answers 0.0% of cases' and p. 19 says it 'refuses all cases', yet Table 7 gives correct abstention 5.0%; different benchmarks, not reconciled. Tables partly jumbled by pdftotext; values read in column order. No LLM or coding agent used in any experiment. Code and artifacts at github.com/PhiniteLab/codex-issue-memory. No pre-registration.
